title: Memory backend endpoints
text: In an AWS deployment of the Intel AI for Enterprise Agent Toolkit, agent memory is served by a single Amazon OpenSearch Service domain. Short-term working context is stored in the agent-session-memory index and long-term knowledge in the agent-knowledge index. Connection details are published in the opensearch-credentials Secret in the opensearch namespace; read the OPENSEARCH_URL key from that Secret rather than hardcoding the endpoint.

title: Reading session state consistently
text: OpenSearch _search is near-real-time with a refresh interval of one second, so a session document that was just written may not appear in search results immediately. To read agent session state with immediate consistency, use the real-time document GET at GET /agent-session-memory/_doc/<id>, which serves from the translog. Do not use _search for read-after-write on session state.

title: Session memory expiry
text: OpenSearch has no per-document time-to-live equivalent to Redis key expiry. The toolkit stamps an expires_at field on session documents and runs a CronJob named opensearch-session-ttl in the opensearch namespace every fifteen minutes. That job issues a _delete_by_query that removes documents whose expires_at has passed, and also removes documents older than the retention window that were written without an expires_at stamp. The default retention window is twenty-four hours.

title: Hybrid retrieval for RAG
text: Retrieval-augmented generation in the toolkit uses hybrid search over the agent-knowledge index, combining k-nearest-neighbour semantic vector matching with BM25 keyword scoring. The two score scales are incompatible, so queries must pass search_pipeline=hybrid-rag-pipeline, which min-max normalises each sub-query score and then combines them with an arithmetic mean weighted seventy percent toward the vector score and thirty percent toward the lexical score.

title: Embedding model and vector dimension
text: The default embedding model for the AWS deployment is amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0, accessed through Amazon Bedrock, which emits vectors of one thousand and twenty-four dimensions. The knn_vector mapping on the agent-knowledge index is fixed at index creation time and cannot be altered afterwards, so changing the embedding model requires deleting and recreating that index. The toolkit validates the returned vector length against the mapping and fails the deployment on a mismatch.

title: Why the control plane runs on CPU
text: The Intel AI for Enterprise Agent Toolkit is built on the observation that an agent spends most of its wall-clock time orchestrating rather than doing model inference. Managing conversation and task state, calling tools, running retrieval, executing generated code, applying guardrails and emitting telemetry are branch-heavy, I/O-bound and highly concurrent, which maps to general-purpose CPU cores rather than accelerators. In the AWS deployment the entire control plane runs on Intel Xeon EC2 instances and reasoning is offloaded to Amazon Bedrock, so no GPU instance is required.

title: Inference gateway entry point
text: All inference in the toolkit goes through the GenAI Gateway, an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM deployment that applies authentication, role-based access control and rate limiting. In-cluster it is reachable at http://genai-gateway-service.genai-gateway.svc.cluster.local:4000/v1. Because every agent framework in the stack, including LangGraph, CrewAI and Flowise, reaches inference through this single endpoint, switching the backing model provider to Amazon Bedrock requires no agent-side code changes.

title: Bedrock model identifiers require an inference-profile prefix
text: Cross-region Amazon Bedrock models must be referenced by their inference-profile identifier, which carries a region-group prefix such as us. For example us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0. Invoking the bare foundation-model identifier without that prefix returns a ValidationException. Because a cross-region inference profile fans out to the underlying foundation model in several regions, the IAM policy must authorise the foundation-model ARN with a wildcard region rather than only the deployment region.

title: Redis instances that remain after the OpenSearch migration
text: Migrating agent memory to Amazon OpenSearch Service retires only the standalone Redis Stack instance that was enabled by deploy_redis. Three other Redis or Valkey instances remain because their consumers speak the Redis protocol and cannot use OpenSearch: the instance bundled with the GenAI Gateway, which holds router state, the response cache and rate-limit counters; the instance bundled with Flowise, which backs its worker queue; and the instance bundled with Langfuse for tracing. Disabling the gateway's Redis breaks usage-based routing and the gateway's startup probe. Eliminating those would mean moving them to Amazon ElastiCache, which is tracked separately.

title: Bedrock model access is separate from IAM
text: Having the correct IAM policy is not sufficient to call an Amazon Bedrock model. Model access is granted per account and per region in the Bedrock console, independently of IAM, so a correct policy still returns AccessDeniedException until access to that specific model has been enabled in that specific region. This is the most common cause of a failed first deployment and is checked by the toolkit's pre-flight validation.

title: Sandboxed code execution
text: Agents in the toolkit execute generated code inside ephemeral Kubernetes sandbox pods, each with its own filesystem and process tree, so a runaway agent cannot affect production systems. The sandbox router is reachable in-cluster at sandbox-router-svc.agent-sandbox.svc.cluster.local:8080 and the default pod template is named python-sandbox-template in the agent-sandbox namespace. The Python SDK is installed with pip install k8s-agent-sandbox.

title: Observability of agent steps
text: Every agent step in the toolkit is traced with Langfuse and metered with Prometheus, Grafana and Loki, all deployed automatically. The GenAI Gateway emits traces through the langfuse_otel callback to the tracing service at http://genai-gateway-trace-web.genai-gateway.svc.cluster.local:3000. Because traces record the model identifier used for each call, the Langfuse view is where you confirm which Amazon Bedrock model served a given reasoning step.
